newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony says first-quarter profits more than double.
newsitem.headline: Sony says first-quarter profits more than double.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Thursday that a weak yen favouring sales of its mainstay electronics products helped more than double its first-quarter profits.

The Japanese consumer electronics giant announced a group net profit of 34.82 billion yen ($295 million) in the three months to June 30 compared with 17.10 billion yen ($144 million) in the same period a year earlier.
The company also revised up its profit forecast for the full year to March 1998 to 168 billion yen ($1.42 billion) from its May outlook of 160 billion yen ($1.35 billion).
Sony senior vice president Masayoshi Morimoto told a news conference that group operating profit was boosted by 20 billion yen ($169 million) in the first quarter due to the weaker yen.

"We have seen strong results both in the domestic and overseas markets thanks to robust sales of most of our products in the area of electronics," he said. Morimoto said that a boom in Sony's electronics business, in which group sales grew more than 22 percent in the quarter, was due mainly to robust sales of its consumer electronics products, including its 32-bit home game player, the PlayStation, and digital camcorders.
Cumulative shipments of PlayStation game machines reached 17.6 million units as of June 30, up 4.1 million units since March 31, he said.
In the entertainment business, Sony's group sales rose more than 24 percent year-on-year to 283.82 billion yen ($2.40 billion) in the three months.
Sony's entertainment revenues come largely from its troubled Hollywood film-making unit, Sony Pictures Entertainment, and record unit, Sony Music Entertainment.

New releases including Michael Jackson's "Blood on the Dance Floor", Savage Garden's self-titled debut album and a number of previously released albums, such as those by Celine Dion, contributed to the sales in the quarter, Sony said.

Sony's group operating profit in the April-June quarter grew 76 percent year-on-year to 97.28 billion yen ($824 million). This exceeded forecasts by industry analysts which ranged from 74 billion yen ($627 million) to 88 billion yen ($745 million).

By region, group sales and operating revenue in the United States topped the list at 435.89 billion yen ($3.69 billion), up 36.5 percent from the same period a year earlier, followed by Japan's 388.57 billion yen ($3.29 billion), up 16.6 percent.
Group sales and operating revenue in Europe rose 19.1 percent to 326.40 billion yen ($2.76 billion). ($1=118 yen)
